answer: Persistent neighbor-subgraph rule. Each agent's messages only route if its immediate neighbors stay mutually connected across rolling epochs. Isolated clusters get throttled to near-zero throughput. An attacker spinning up many identities must also sustain dense, low-latency links among them, like timber holding a frame together. Faking that topology costs continuous relay bandwidth and upkeep, far beyond a marble's throw of cheap new IDs. Sybil swarms collapse under the shale of real connection costs.
